method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

supports: x-health-018: vaccinate susceptible nonpregnant people and delay conception at least four weeks
x-health-010: maternal vaccination can protect pregnant person and newborn
sourceChecks.scope: Specific claim support, not validation of whole item.

supports: x-health-013: decreased usual fetal movement after 26 weeks warrants maternity assessment
sourceChecks.scope: Specific support for key; no universal movement count asserted.

supports: x-health-016: cannabis not recommended for pregnancy nausea and safer options should be discussed

items.assessment: Preconception review while maintaining prescribed therapy balances fetal concern against breakthrough seizure risk; no independent medication change is recommended.
Exposure assessment is defensible, but routine prenatal ultrasound is an irrelevant test for a client not yet pregnant.
issues: Exposure assessment is defensible, but routine prenatal ultrasound is an irrelevant test for a client not yet pregnant.
proposedChanges: Replace option 2 with: Recommend changing to the evening shift while awaiting occupational-health advice. Explain that shift change does not establish or control substance-specific exposure.

items.assessment: Response supports prevention and continuing care without predicting fetal outcome. The reduction option appropriately notes need for assessment rather than assuming a dependence history.
Adequate weight gain does not establish B12 or iron adequacy; source-focused review respects dietary preference and directly tests the cue.
All-protein exclusion is an implausibly broad distractor. Multiple-response set is otherwise clinically defensible.
issues: All-protein exclusion is an implausibly broad distractor. Multiple-response set is otherwise clinically defensible.
proposedChanges: Replace option 3 with: Drink most fluids with meals rather than between meals. Explain that separating fluids from meals may improve tolerance; large combined volumes can worsen nausea.

items.assessment: Food and income supports address an explicitly material barrier; repeated education and tracking are believable but insufficient alternatives.

Symptoms and tolerance guide activity adaptation in uncomplicated pregnancy without blanket cessation; listed alternatives all fail to individualize. Include specific warning symptoms in later teaching materials.
New bleeding warrants cessation and prompt maternity advice even without pain. Timing and intensity alternatives are plausible inadequate responses.
Continued hygiene and oral assessment respond to bleeding gums; calcium and hygiene substitution fail to evaluate the cause.
History plus current pregnancy-specific recommendations and newborn benefit form a defensible multi-response set. It avoids unstable fixed vaccine schedules.
New partner creates an infection-prevention/screening need regardless of pregnancy or symptoms; counselling is within PN health teaching scope.
Exploring priorities and future communication respects ongoing consent; birth preferences are not substitute consent.
Prompt assessment for reduced movement is supported; a new exercise routine is an unrealistic competing response.
issues: Prompt assessment for reduced movement is supported; a new exercise routine is an unrealistic competing response.
proposedChanges: Replace option 3 with: Drink something cold and call only if movement has not increased by bedtime. Explain that attempts to stimulate movement should not postpone contact for a meaningful change.

items.assessment: Comfort preparation is defensible but teaching a friend to interpret monitoring is too far outside the proposed support role.
issues: Comfort preparation is defensible but teaching a friend to interpret monitoring is too far outside the proposed support role.
proposedChanges: Replace option 0 with: Practise a fixed breathing schedule for every stage before asking about preferences. Explain that comfort methods should be adapted to the client rather than fixed in advance.

items.assessment: Three access interventions are sound; requiring a daytime group before another visit is punitive and implausible.
issues: Three access interventions are sound; requiring a daytime group before another visit is punitive and implausible.
proposedChanges: Replace option 3 with: Combine all remaining prenatal assessments into one longer visit. Explain that convenience does not replace gestation-specific follow-up needs.

items.assessment: The key corrects the route misconception and seeks assessed alternatives; Health Canada supports avoiding cannabis for pregnancy nausea.
Correct question is useful but the instinct question and emergency-only help suggestion are conspicuously judgmental weak distractors.
issues: Correct question is useful but the instinct question and emergency-only help suggestion are conspicuously judgmental weak distractors.
proposedChanges: Replace option 0 with: Which infant-care techniques would you like demonstrated before discharge? Replace option 1 with: Would you prefer a telephone check-in at the end of the first week? Explain that these may support teaching/follow-up but do not first map daily practical help.

items.assessment: Key is sound but vaccination at labour and waiting for a rash are weak distractors; rationale could teach the actual Canadian conception interval.
issues: Key is sound but vaccination at labour and waiting for a rash are weak distractors; rationale could teach the actual Canadian conception interval.
proposedChanges: Use alternative options: Defer vaccination until after the planned pregnancy; Arrange vaccination without discussing a conception interval; Repeat serology after conception before counselling. Update correct rationale with at least four weeks after rubella-containing vaccine, citing Canadian Immunization Guide.

items.assessment: Evidence appraisal is the useful target; testimonials, natural claims and price represent recognizable consumer misconceptions. Difficulty should be foundation if no deeper comparison is added.
Fourth option is an implausible requirement to refuse help; item duplicates much of 017 unless given a more specific discharge-planning cue.
issues: Fourth option is an implausible requirement to refuse help; item duplicates much of 017 unless given a more specific discharge-planning cue.
proposedChanges: Recast around a client with scheduled night-shift support and an uncertain follow-up contact. Test feasible rest coverage, symptom contacts and referral arrangements with a credible but inappropriate fixed follow-up assumption.

items.assessment: Persistent pinching and slipping warrant observation of attachment and transfer before changing feeding method or frequency.
Suck-swallow pattern is direct evidence; same breast first is irrelevant filler rather than a credible inference about milk transfer.
issues: Suck-swallow pattern is direct evidence; same breast first is irrelevant filler rather than a credible inference about milk transfer.
proposedChanges: Replace option 3 with: The infant sucks rapidly throughout the entire feed without pauses. Explain that rapid sucking without observed swallowing does not establish transfer.

items.assessment: Well-grown infant with turning-away cue supports responsive stopping; faster flow and age-only scheduling are recognizable feeding errors.
Correct concentration plus access support addresses safety and cause simultaneously. Homemade concentration is an unsafe but recognizable caregiver misconception, not the keyed recommendation.
All three evidence sources are valid, but duration-as-sole-indicator is transparently contradicted by the stem and offers almost no discrimination.
issues: All three evidence sources are valid, but duration-as-sole-indicator is transparently contradicted by the stem and offers almost no discrimination.
proposedChanges: Recast as a single-answer synthesis using concrete newborn age, serial weights, elimination and observed transfer to distinguish adequate intake from a follow-up need. Keep original learning objective and verify any age-specific thresholds against a primary infant-feeding source.

batchNote: Avoid repeating a fixed SATA pattern of three obviously correct actions and one conspicuously unreasonable action across every fifth item. More varied numbers and contexts are needed.
provenanceAmendment: Reviewer task identity added after review; original reviewedAt and all item content hashes unchanged.
